systemAudioHelp.title: Capturing system audio
systemAudioHelp.fullSupport: Full system-audio capture is supported. When you click System audio or Microphone + system, pick Entire Screen in the share dialog and check Share system audio.
systemAudioHelp.tabAudioOnly: This browser can't record system audio on this operating system. You can still record tab audio by sharing a tab that plays sound, or route system audio through a virtual audio device. Steps are below.
systemAudioHelp.noSupport: This browser can't record audio from a screen share. Use Chrome or Edge to record system audio, or record from a microphone.
systemAudioHelp.macIntro: macOS doesn't let browsers record system audio directly. The usual workaround is a free virtual audio driver: with it, system output appears as an input the browser can use like a microphone.
systemAudioHelp.macA1: Open the source content in a tab (YouTube, Zoom web, etc.)
systemAudioHelp.macA2: Click System Audio in Speakr and pick the tab in the share dialog
systemAudioHelp.tickShareTabAudio: Check Share tab audio before clicking Share
systemAudioHelp.macANote: Works only for content playing in a browser tab. App audio (Slack, native Zoom client, etc.) won't be captured.
systemAudioHelp.macB1: Install {{link}} (free). The installer signs in with no kernel-extension prompts.
systemAudioHelp.macB2: Open Audio MIDI Setup → create a Multi-Output Device containing your speakers + BlackHole. Set this as the system output.
systemAudioHelp.macB3: In Speakr, click Microphone and pick BlackHole 2ch as the input.
systemAudioHelp.macBNote: Once set up, system audio is recorded whichever tab or window is active.
systemAudioHelp.winIntro: On Windows, Chrome and Edge can record any audio the system plays, including a single app. No extra software is needed.
systemAudioHelp.win1: Click System audio or Microphone + system in Speakr
systemAudioHelp.win2: In the share dialog, pick Entire Screen
systemAudioHelp.win3: Check Share system audio (bottom-left of the dialog)
systemAudioHelp.winWNote: Only that app's audio is recorded, so your typing stays out of meeting recordings.
systemAudioHelp.winStuck: Stuck on "no audio track" errors? Some apps (Spotify desktop, DRM-protected video) suppress system-audio capture. Use a virtual cable like {{link}} as a workaround.
systemAudioHelp.linuxIntro: On Linux, pick the option that fits what you want to record:
systemAudioHelp.linuxA1: Play the source content in a Chrome tab (YouTube, Zoom web, meeting URL, etc.)
systemAudioHelp.linuxA2: Click System Audio in Speakr, then pick that tab in the share dialog
systemAudioHelp.linuxPavucontrolNote: This won't show up in pavucontrol. Chrome captures tab audio internally and never routes through PulseAudio, so the Recording tab will say "No application is currently recording audio." That's normal: Speakr's meter is the source of truth.
systemAudioHelp.linuxANote: Only captures audio playing inside a browser tab. Native apps (Slack, Spotify desktop, Discord) won't be picked up.
systemAudioHelp.linuxOptionB: Option B. Switch source in pavucontrol mid-recording
systemAudioHelp.linuxBIntro: Quick, but system audio replaces your microphone. Use it to record what's playing without your voice.
systemAudioHelp.linuxB3: Change Speakr's capture source from your mic to Monitor of <your output>
systemAudioHelp.linuxOptionC: Option C. Expose a virtual source so Chrome will list it (recommended)
systemAudioHelp.linuxCWhy: Why this is needed: In Chrome on Linux, "Monitor of …" sources are hidden from web apps, so they are missing from Speakr's input list even though they appear in pavucontrol. A regular virtual source wrapped around a monitor is not hidden. The new source then appears in Speakr, as the main input or under "Also mix in" beside your microphone.
systemAudioHelp.linuxCFindSink: Find your output sink name (the part before {{suffix}}):
systemAudioHelp.linuxCWrap: Then wrap its monitor as a virtual source Chrome will list:
systemAudioHelp.linuxCReload: Reload Speakr's input-device picker. You'll now see speakr_loopback in the dropdown. Pick it as "Also mix in" alongside your real mic and you'll capture both.
systemAudioHelp.linuxCPersist: To persist across reboots, add the {{line}} line to {{file}}.
systemAudioHelp.pipewireBody: Same idea. Wrap the monitor in a virtual source so Chrome doesn't filter it. Use {{tool}}: {{command}}. Or use {{qpwgraph}} / {{helvum}} to wire it visually.
systemAudioHelp.detectedIntro: These virtual devices are already set up on this computer:
systemAudioHelp.detectedPick: Pick this from the microphone dropdown to capture system audio.
systemAudioHelp.privacyIntro: Most of these modes use standard browser APIs, with the same privacy as any web app that records audio. Two have trade-offs, described below.
systemAudioHelp.privacyMicBody: Browser permission is required for each. You're asked before recording starts, an indicator shows while it runs, and you can revoke access in the site settings.
systemAudioHelp.privacyProcessingBody: These are audio-quality processors, not privacy controls. With them off the recording captures more of the ambient room (background voices, typing, notifications).
systemAudioHelp.privacyVirtualBody: On any system, a virtual audio device shows up in {{api}} beside your real microphone. Any site with microphone permission can choose it and record whatever plays through it, under the normal "recording" indicator, not the "screen sharing" one.
systemAudioHelp.privacyMac: macOS (BlackHole / Loopback). The device is a permanently installed audio driver. The risk is active only while system audio is actually routed through it, i.e. while your output is set to the Multi-Output Device you configured. When you're not recording, switch the system output back to your normal device so nothing flows through BlackHole.
systemAudioHelp.privacyWindows: Windows (VB-Cable, Voicemeeter, Stereo Mix). Same pattern. The risk is active while audio is routed through the cable. Native "Share system audio" via the share dialog has no comparable exposure because nothing is routed through a virtual mic.
systemAudioHelp.privacyLinux: Linux ({{loopback}}). Chrome's filtering of "Monitor of …" sources is a deliberate privacy protection. The {{module}} wrap explicitly undoes that protection. Unlike macOS/Windows the device is a runtime PulseAudio module you can load and unload at will.
systemAudioHelp.mitigationRoute: Route system audio through the virtual device only while recording. On macOS, switch the system output back to your speakers / headphones after. On Windows, stop routing audio through the cable. On Linux, {{unload}} after, or don't put the {{load}} line in {{file}}.
systemAudioHelp.mitigationAudit: Audit your mic permissions at {{url}} and remove any site that doesn't strictly need it.
systemAudioHelp.mitigationRename: Use a less obvious device name where you can choose one (e.g. {{example}} instead of {{loopback}} on Linux). It won't stop a determined site, but it helps.
systemAudioHelp.whereBody: Audio goes to this Speakr server, then to the transcription service set up for it. With a local Whisper or self-hosted ASR, audio stays on your network. With OpenAI or another cloud provider, audio is sent there.

whatsNew.titleSince: What's new since your last visit

0_10_20.1: Choose a new look: six interface themes under Account settings → Preferences → Appearance, each with your color scheme and dark mode.
0_10_20.2: The chat and Inquire are now Ambrose, an assistant you can rename. Click a citation number to play that moment.
0_10_20.3: Each recording keeps its own chat until you close the tab.
0_10_20.4: Folders can hold subfolders. Choose a parent folder when you create or edit a folder.
0_10_20.5: In Regenerate summary, you see the prompt that will run and can edit it first.
0_10_20.6: Follow a translation's progress in the processing queue and the Translation tab.
0_10_20.7: Download a summary as Markdown, and single answers or whole Ask Ambrose conversations as Word documents.

0_10_21.1: You can connect apps that sign you in with the same single sign-on as Speakr, such as Open WebUI, without copying an API token, once an admin turns this on.
0_10_21.2: Ambrose finds a person by a first name, a surname or another spelling, and searches every name the person appears under.
0_10_21.3: A long Sources list under an answer is folded. Click Sources to open it.
0_10_21.4: If you missed several updates, you see what's new in each of them.
0_10_21.5: Signing out from a page that was open for a long time works.
